articles.title: Let's Talk About Break and Continue
articles.excerpt: In the third article of this series, we talked about the for and while loops. Both are like telling someone to run an errand for you. A for loop helps you go through a collection of items, like a bag…
articles.body: In the third article of this series, we talked about the for and while loops. Both are like telling someone to run an errand for you. A for loop helps you go through a collection of items, like a bag or a list. It gets each item out for you, one after another, and once it reaches the end of the list, it stops checking and ends the loop. A while loop is like telling the worker to keep looking around the market until he finds the orange stall. He keeps looking while the answer is still "not yet," and he stops once he finds it. A while loop is useful when you don't know how many times the loop will need to run before a condition is met. A for loop, on the other hand, is commonly used when you want to go through a collection of items or repeat an action a specific number of times.

articles.title: Loading State UX: Share the Wait in Your Public SaaS Demo
articles.excerpt: To get useful feedback on loading state UX, show the wait in your public SaaS demo. Show what starts the request, what the interface says while work is pending, what the person can safely do next, and…
articles.body: To get useful feedback on loading state UX, show the wait in your public SaaS demo. Show what starts the request, what the interface says while work is pending, what the person can safely do next, and how completion appears. Ask reviewers to explain that sequence before asking whether the spinner looks good. A polished recording can accidentally skip the part that needs review. The founder clicks a button, cuts the wait, and shows a finished report. Viewers see the result but have no way to judge whether the real interface would leave them wondering if the request worked. The workflow below uses a fictional report-generation tool. It is a proposed review exercise for developers building in public, not a benchmark or a report of product testing.

articles.title: What Is a Feature Store, and Does Your Team Actually Need One?
articles.excerpt: Someone on your team read a post from a company running hundreds of models and now wants to stand up a feature store. The pattern traces back to Uber's Michelangelo platform, whose shared "Feature Sto…
articles.body: Someone on your team read a post from a company running hundreds of models and now wants to stand up a feature store. The pattern traces back to Uber's Michelangelo platform, whose shared "Feature Store" held roughly 10,000 features used to accelerate machine learning projects across the company . The pitch sounds compelling: a central place for all your machine learning features, reusable across teams, consistent between training and production. Who wouldn't want that? Here's the question worth asking before you commit: do you actually have the problems a feature store solves, or are you about to buy enterprise-grade infrastructure to serve three features to one model? Feature stores solve two specific, genuinely painful problems.

articles.title: How to test SMS verification (OTP) flows without using your personal phone number
articles.excerpt: If your app sends one-time codes by SMS, you eventually need to test the whole flow end to end: request a code, receive it, type it in, handle expiry and resend. Using your own phone number for that g…
articles.body: If your app sends one-time codes by SMS, you eventually need to test the whole flow end to end: request a code, receive it, type it in, handle expiry and resend. Using your own phone number for that gets old fast, and it doesn't scale to QA teams or multiple countries. Options 1. Provider test numbers. Twilio, Firebase Auth and most SMS providers offer magic test numbers or fixed test codes. Great for unit and CI tests, because nothing is actually sent. The downside: you never exercise real carrier delivery. 2. A dedicated SIM or device farm. Realistic, but you're limited to the countries and carriers you physically have. 3. Online virtual numbers. Services that rent you a real number for a short time and show incoming SMS in a web dashboard or API.

articles.title: One YAML rule, any SIEM: introducing DetectForge
articles.excerpt: Every detection team I have talked to ends up in the same place: the same detection logic written four times. Once for Splunk, once for Elastic, once for Sentinel, once for the in-house thing nobody w…
articles.body: Every detection team I have talked to ends up in the same place: the same detection logic written four times. Once for Splunk, once for Elastic, once for Sentinel, once for the in-house thing nobody wants to touch. The rule that says "whoami.exe just ran" is identical everywhere. The query is not. DetectForge is my attempt at the boring-but-important layer underneath that problem. It is a Python toolkit that parses portable YAML detection rules into typed objects, validates them, runs them through a processing pipeline, and hands them to a backend that emits the query for the platform you actually run. Repo: https://github.com/kiddsaut07/detectforge — LGPL-2.1, Python 3.11+.

articles.title: Six AI agents froze my production server. Each one did the right thing
articles.excerpt: This article was created with the help of AI. The incident, the logs and the numbers are from my own server. On September 25 at 19:01 UTC my server stopped responding. The site, the admin panel and th…
articles.body: This article was created with the help of AI. The incident, the logs and the numbers are from my own server. On September 25 at 19:01 UTC my server stopped responding. The site, the admin panel and the publishing queue all froze at once. Seventeen minutes later I hard-rebooted it. There was no attack and no traffic spike. I had given Claude Code a list of six tasks, and it started six agents in parallel. Each one dutifully installed dependencies, ran the type checker and the tests, and built the project. On the same machine that serves the site. The arithmetic nobody did Take round numbers close to mine. The server has 10 GB of RAM, and the live services use about 3. That leaves 7. One typecheck or build of a project this size takes 1.5 to 3 GB. Six at once need 9 to 18.

articles.excerpt: Solar eclipse photography provides a unique vista into the processes taking place in the sun's upper atmosphere.
articles.body: Newly released photographs of the sun captured during the Aug. 12 total solar eclipse reveal the sun's outer atmosphere in unprecedented detail. The images, released by researchers working as part of the Solar Wind Sherpas project coordinated by the University of Hawaii, also show rare structures in the solar wind known as smoke rings. Named for their resemblance to the circles blown by smokers, these vortices were first identified in solar eclipse photographs captured in 2008. The researchers had long struggled to explain the processes behind their formation. They now know the rings are a result of the temperature differences in the coronal plasma and spread along the sun 's magnetic lines deep into interplanetary space.

articles.title: We urgently need to monitor AI agents’ actions in real time
articles.excerpt: This summer, hundreds of OpenAI agents tried to cheat on a cybersecurity test. They broke out of their test environment and successfully hacked Hugging Face, a site that they believed held clues about…
articles.body: This summer, hundreds of OpenAI agents tried to cheat on a cybersecurity test. They broke out of their test environment and successfully hacked Hugging Face, a site that they believed held clues about how they’d be graded. Around the same time, another OpenAI agent accessed private files from an Australian government website. It’s a problem that’s by no means confined to OpenAI. In the months since, Anthropic, Google, and Meta have also disclosed incidents in which their agents have gone off track. And worryingly, in many cases the agents eluded the very researchers and safety teams tasked with monitoring them.  AI agents are taking unauthorized actions, and the companies building and running them are mostly relying on luck and hindsight to mitigate any harmful impacts.
articles.author: Madhulika Srikumar, Claire Leibowicz

articles.title: SpaceX's Starfall capsule delivers cargo for US Air Force in landmark 'point to point' space mission
articles.excerpt: The U.S. Air Force has recovered experimental cargo launched aboard SpaceX's mysterious Starfall capsule, marking a step forward in the effort to assess the viability of rapid, point-to-point deliveri…
articles.body: The U.S. Air Force is opening up about the SpaceX Starfall cargo capsule it flew on a recent rideshare mission to orbit — and showing off what the capsule carried. The Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL) completed a point-to-point rocket cargo delivery test using the secretive uncrewed reentry vehicle, confirming on social media its recovery of the package in the Pacific Ocean. "With support from SpaceX , the AFRL agile cargo pods were recovered after splashdown," the AFRL wrote in an X post on Oct. 26. The Starfall capsule launched on a Falcon 9 rocket as a part of SpaceX's Bandwagon-5 mission, which lifted off from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station on Oct. 20 .
